comparator.name: Bachelor Fiscaal Recht
comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from the official 2025-2026 Teaching and Examination Regulations for the Bachelor Fiscaal Recht. This is the latest complete programme-specific regulation publicly discoverable on the EUR site during production. Article 6 fixes the degree at 180 EC; Articles 10 and 11 name every component and define the credit-letter key. The result is three 60-EC years: a 60-EC legal and fiscal foundation year, a 60-EC second year combining tax, private law, company law, public finance, accounting and legal-academic skills, and a 60-EC third year containing a 15-EC minor, five 7-EC advanced legal or tax components, and a 10-EC legal-academic-skills component that includes the bachelor thesis. Current public programme pages were used for descriptive corroboration. No 2026-2027 programme-specific OER was discoverable, and no change from the published 2025-2026 credit structure is inferred.
components: Introduction to International and European Union Law
Open minor component of at least 15 EC, subject to the programme's approval rules.
Advanced fiscal legal-academic skills component that includes the independent bachelor thesis.

candidates.label: Public, international and European law and policy

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the programme's generic tax-law identity, legal analysis, private-law foundation, legal communication and independent-research interests. Two additional generator-backed directions remain. The relationship between tax law, business and company organisation supports a business, finance and commercial-regulation route. International and European tax law together with administrative law and government powers supports a public, international and European law-and-policy route. Both are feasible and qualitatively distinct. The closest match differs from each related direction by six courses; the two related directions differ by eleven. Both additional candidates are included, reaching the maximum of three alternatives.

alternatives.label: Law, economics & public finance
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines the strongest available UCR law sequence with economics, public finance, accounting, business law, EU institutions and legal communication. The label states those available fields and does not imply that UCR offers a tax-law degree.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response combines broad legal foundations and public, private, international, EU, criminal and business law with economics, taxation and public-spending analysis, accounting, finance, empirical research and persuasive legal communication.
progression: Law, Society & Justice in semester 1 precedes every later course that formally requires it. Research Methods & Statistics precedes all selected economics courses with that prerequisite, while Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations precedes Transnational Business Law, International Business & Governance and Money, Banking & Finance. Introductory economics precedes the advanced economics sequence conceptually. The Art of Rhetorical Communication precedes Rhetoric in Action. The final year concentrates advanced private law, EU politics, governance, econometrics, finance and qualitative research. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternatives.label: Business, finance & commercial regulation
alternatives.labelReason: The route concentrates the programme's company-law, business-organisation, financial-reporting and commercial dimensions in a business-and-economics sequence with supporting international and private law. The label avoids claiming tax-law coverage that UCR cannot provide.
alternatives.concept: A commercially oriented route in which business organisation, accounting, finance, strategy, organisational leadership, market research and economics are combined with private, international and transnational business law and applied communication.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route removes criminal law, constitutional and administrative law, EU law, EU politics, international-relations theory and qualitative social research. It adds digital business strategy, organisational leadership, business and regulation in the age of AI, behavioural economics, market research and applied rhetoric. Six of the 24 courses differ, and the organising choice shifts from a broad law-and-public-finance comparison to business organisation, commercial decision-making and finance.
progression: Law, Society & Justice, Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations and Introduction to Economics establish the legal, business and economic strands in semester 1. Research Methods & Statistics precedes all selected courses that formally require it; Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations precedes Strategy & Digital Transformation, Transnational Business Law, International Business & Governance, Money, Banking & Finance and Market Research. The Art of Rhetorical Communication precedes Persuasive Communication. The final year advances from accounting, macroeconomics and organisational leadership to private law, global governance, finance, econometrics, behavioural economics and independent market research. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternatives.label: Public, international & European law
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum centres public authority, constitutional and administrative law, international and EU law, EU politics and public economics, with sociology and research methods supplying the societal context. It is explicitly a related legal direction rather than a tax-law substitute.
alternatives.concept: A public-law and policy route connecting constitutional and administrative authority, international and EU legal orders, human rights and criminal justice with EU politics, international relations, public economics, sociology and empirical research.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route removes the business-foundations, accounting, international-business, macroeconomics, finance and transnational-business-law courses. It adds sociology, modern and contemporary social theory, political philosophy, peace and conflict, and behavioural economics. Six of the 24 courses differ from the closest match and eleven differ from the business direction. The route is therefore organised around public authority, institutions and society rather than commercial practice.
progression: Law, Society & Justice, Introduction to Economics and Introduction to Sociology establish the legal, economic and social foundations in semester 1. Law, Society & Justice precedes every later law course with that formal prerequisite, and Research Methods & Statistics precedes all selected advanced economics courses. International law, constitutional law and international-relations theory precede the advanced EU-law, EU-politics and conflict courses conceptually. Introductory rhetoric precedes Rhetoric in Action, and introductory sociology precedes advanced contemporary social theory conceptually. The final semester brings together qualitative methodology, econometrics, behavioural economics and applied public communication. Every course is available in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

blocks: Both introduce the nature, sources and social operation of law; UCR does so through legal, social and normative perspectives.
Both establish private-law rights and obligations; UCR surveys property, contract, family and related private-law relationships.
Both examine constitutional and administrative institutions, public powers, legal limits and protected rights.
Both introduce substantive criminal-law reasoning and criminal justice, including accountability and legal safeguards.
Both introduce international legal sources, institutions and treaty relationships; the comparator also integrates introductory EU law.
Both address the legal organisation and regulation of business, although UCR concentrates on transnational commercial transactions rather than Dutch company law.

UCR's Principles of Private Law includes contracts and obligations within a broader survey, but the same UCR course is already aligned to the comparator's introductory private-law component; there is no second dedicated obligations-law course.
UCR's private-law survey includes property but not a dedicated property-rights and insolvency course of the comparator's depth.

Comparative Constitutional Law includes administrative-law foundations but is already aligned to the first-year combined constitutional and administrative component; UCR has no separate advanced administrative-law course.
UCR has no course in tax procedure, assessment, enforcement or taxpayers' procedural protection.
Both provide an economic and societal frame for understanding legal rules and government policy; UCR supplies the economics foundation directly.
Both teach accounting and financial-statement analysis, but UCR does not add the comparator's fiscal-accounting applications.
Both examine government revenue and spending; UCR explicitly covers taxation, public expenditure, redistribution, efficiency and equity.
UCR Public Economics analyses taxation economically but does not teach the legal system, sources and doctrines of Dutch tax law.
UCR has no dedicated course on municipal taxes or local-government levies.
UCR has no dedicated Dutch income-tax and payroll-tax course.
UCR has no course on the fiscal calculation of taxable business profits.
UCR has no dedicated corporate-income-tax course.
UCR offers international and EU law and global business governance, but not the substantive international and European tax-law component.
UCR has no dedicated course on turnover tax or the European VAT system.
Both teach empirical investigation of law and society; UCR concentrates on qualitative design, data collection, interpretation and dissemination.
Both develop academic argument, writing and oral presentation; UCR teaches these through rhetoric rather than specifically fiscal legal documents.
Both advance oral argument and communication through applied work; UCR uses public speaking and debate rather than fiscal legal advocacy.

The comparator requires advanced fiscal legal-academic skills and an independent bachelor thesis. None of the 24 scheduled UCR courses is a thesis, so the component is unmatched and UCR's optional independent-research element is displayed alongside it.

The comparator's 15-EC minor is an open choice rather than a fixed academic subject. UCR flexibility is distributed across the entire 180-EC plan, so no single scheduled course is asserted as its equivalent.

notes.text: The Rotterdam programme is a professional academic law degree with a continuous, jurisdiction-specific sequence in Dutch tax law: introductory tax law, local levies, income tax, taxable profit, formal tax procedure, corporate income tax, international and European tax law, and VAT, supported by Dutch private, public and company law and a fiscal legal thesis. UCR can combine public economics and taxation analysis with broad private, public, criminal, international, EU and business law, accounting, finance and research methods. It does not teach the Dutch tax code, tax returns, fiscal procedure or the named specialist taxes. These pathways therefore compare related legal, economic and institutional fields; none reproduces the external tax-law discipline or its professional qualification path.
